speech_en: Touchdown! Special delivery for E. coli!
speech_de: Landung geglückt! Sonderlieferung für E. coli!
scenario: A cheerful little moon-lander-shaped bacteriophage character (a rounded, elongated capsule head like a friendly rocket nose cone, big happy cartoon eyes, sitting on a short round collar/body) touches down gently on top of a big round smiling bacterium-planet character standing in for E. coli. The phage rests on six short, blunt, rounded landing-leg bumps tucked under its body like a toy lunar lander's feet — not spikes, not rays, not a starburst. With one stubby rounded arm it hands the bacterium character a small rolled-up scroll (its DNA) through a little open hatch on the bacterium's side; both are smiling, no force, no bursting, no fight. Mirrors the set's 'show the friendly mechanism, not menace' convention and the lentiviral-vector precedent (renders/set/engineered-life/lentiviral-vector.coloring.prompt.json) for turning spikes/tail fibres into blunt rounded studs to avoid a starburst — the single riskiest failure mode named in SKILL.md for anything radiating from a hub.

prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080.

THIS IS A MACRO CLOSE-UP SHOT, LIKE A ZOOMED-IN PHONE CAMERA PHOTO TAKEN TOO CLOSE. The subject is so close to the "camera" that it does NOT fully fit in the frame: the top of the phage character's head is CUT OFF by the TOP edge, the round bacterium-planet character is CUT OFF by the LEFT, RIGHT and BOTTOM edges. There must be ZERO empty white background space visible anywhere in the image — every part of the 1080x1080 canvas is covered by either black line-art or white space that belongs INSIDE a drawn shape. If you can see plain empty background at any edge, the drawing is WRONG — redo it bigger and closer.

SCENE (draw it oversized, then let the frame crop it): A cheerful little bacteriophage character shaped like a friendly toy moon-lander: a rounded, elongated capsule head (a soft-cornered hexagonal capsule shape, longer than it is wide, NOT a perfect circle) with big happy cartoon eyes and a big smile, sitting on a short round collar that connects to a short stubby body. Under the body, SIX SHORT, BLUNT, ROUNDED landing-leg bumps rest gently on the surface below — like the rounded rubber feet of a toy lander, evenly spaced, each one short and stubby, touching a big round smiling bacterium-planet character (standing in for E. coli, drawn as a giant friendly circle/oval with a cheerful little face and a small open hatch/door on its side). With one short rounded arm, the phage character hands a small rolled-up scroll (its DNA delivery, tied with a little bow) through the bacterium's open hatch. Both characters are smiling. No fight, no forcing, no bursting, no popping — the hatch is already open and welcoming. Keep the background almost bare aside from two or three simple rounded sparkle-free dots near the scroll — no other objects.

STYLE — coloring book line art: BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed. NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black fills anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only). Simple, cheerful, chunky shapes with open white space INSIDE each shape for colouring.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN:
- Any visible empty white background, wall, sky or margin space — the artwork must be so zoomed-in and oversized that it touches or crosses every one of the four edges, with elements literally cut off by the edges.
- ANY starburst, radiating burst, sparkle rays, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, or a halo of rays anywhere — this applies especially to the six landing legs, which must be SHORT, BLUNT and ROUNDED, tucked close under the body, never long, never pointed, never drawn as spikes or thin rays fanning out from a hub.
- More or fewer than six landing-leg bumps, or legs of uneven, spiky, or thread-like shape.
- ANY rectangle, box outline, picture frame, panel edge, border line or vignette around the whole picture.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks.
- NO speech bubble or thought bubble (added separately afterwards).
- NO fighting, no bursting/popping cell, no bite marks, no blood, no medical tools, no sick or sad character, no needles.
- NO full human figure or human face anywhere.
- The phage character never bites, stings or forces its way in — the hatch is already open and welcoming, and the whole scene is a gentle, happy delivery.
